newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Westpac shares climb after profit rise.
newsitem.headline: Westpac shares climb after profit rise.

text.p: Westpac Banking Corp shares rose into positive territory on Wednesday after the bank announced a 12.9 percent rise in first half net profit to A$638 million.

At 2.00 p.m. (0400 GMT), Westpac shares were six cents firmer at A$7.56, having touched an intraday high after the announcement of A$7.60. Prior to the announcement, Westpac shares stood unchanged from Tuesday's close at A$7.50.
Brokers said the result had been well-received, reflecting the recent investor faith placed in the sector.

"The bank sector continues to run on very strongly. Westpac shot to a high of A$7.60 but have settled back now," said a Brisbane-based brokerage, adding that the stocks had finding buyers around its current levels.
"They seem to be finding support around that A$7.53-A$7.55 level."

The bank also said it planned to raise up to A$500 million through a preference share issue, the proceeds of which would be used to fund its merger deal with Victorian-based regional bank, Bank of Melbourne.
Westpac bid values Bank of Melbourne at A$1.435 billion ar about A$9.75 per share but the merger plan is subject to approval by the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission.
By 2.40 p.m. (0440 GMT), Westpac shares were three cents higher at A$7.53 on turnover of 1.98 million shares.
